_doc: Point-in-time fact sheet for CMCSA retrospectives (retro/build_cmcsa.py). Every value is tied to a source and becomes visible only on or after that source's 'published' date. A filing accepted after the 16:00 ET close is dated the next trading day ('filed' keeps the acceptance time, US Eastern; EDGAR gives only the filing date before 2003); the earnings 8-Ks of 2007-2009 were accepted before the open on their release days. The builder uses the latest history vintage published by AS_OF, the prints published by AS_OF that report a fiscal year after that history (a Q4 print reports the year just ended and extends the history until the 10-K), the guides for the current fiscal year (each field from the latest guide that states it) and the latest declared dividend (else the vintage's). Comcast's fiscal year is the calendar year. EPS is diluted EPS from continuing operations, replaced by the company's adjusted figure where it excludes only one-offs (2006-2008). 2003 is excluded and the history starts with 2004. Guides: consolidated revenue growth in percent, pro forma, as stated; Comcast guides no EPS and no operating margin. A print's growth and margins are derived from the raw figures of its release ('raw', $ millions and thousands of subscribers; the builder re-derives and checks them), each against the year-ago quarter as the same release shows it. Rule T's raw figures are in 'rule_t'. A Q4 print may restate an earlier year's EPS ('restates', from the release that first publishes it) until a 10-K vintage published after it carries the year. No later fact enters through this file.

rule_t._doc: Rule T (retro/README.md, LOW and CMCSA): for each signal its annual values for fiscal 1997-2006, each change from the latest 10-K published by 2008-01-04 whose statements (or, for subscribers, whose cable operating table) report both years; XBULL = the decade's best, BULL = its median, BASE = its worst, BEAR = one median-to-worst step beyond the worst (mirrored for capital intensity, where lower is better); rounded half up to whole percent and to 10 bp. Seams stay in, as published: QVC is consolidated until the FY2003 10-K presents it as discontinued (the 2002 change is QVC-free), Comcast Cellular is discontinued from the FY1999 10-K, the FY2000 10-K reclassifies electronic-retailing revenue, acquisitions (Jones, Lenfest, the AT&T exchanges, AT&T Broadband in November 2002, Adelphia and Time Warner in 2006) enter with the filings that report them, franchise amortization stops in 2002, and the FY2006 10-K excludes the systems transferred to Time Warner from every year of its cable table. The builder re-derives every value and threshold from the raw figures and refuses to build if they differ.

price_basis: Yahoo's CMCSA series is adjusted for the 2-for-1 split of 2017-02-21 and a factor of 1.067 dated 2026-01-05 (Yahoo's split event for that date, the Versant Media distribution); every date here precedes both, so the builder multiplies Yahoo's close by their product (2.134) and gets the price as traded: $18.26 on 2007-12-31 and $16.88 on 2008-12-31. The 3-for-2 split of 2007-02-22 precedes every date: prices before it are on the post-split basis in Yahoo's series, as are the per-share facts (the 'splits' record restates the Q4 2006 release's $0.90).

distributions.note: the Versant Media spin-off; Yahoo records it as a 1067:1000 split. It follows every date here and enters only through the price basis
